goal: Ship a local desktop app with two independent terminal panes, each capable of running the Codex CLI.

tasks.title: Define the v1 scope and acceptance criteria
acceptance_criteria: The supported operating system for v1 is documented.
The app is confirmed to be local-only and single-user.
Out-of-scope features are documented, including linked agents, extra CLI tools, accounts, and cloud sync.

tasks.title: Choose the desktop application stack
acceptance_criteria: The UI framework, desktop shell, terminal emulator, and PTY library are selected.
The selected stack can create and control two interactive shell processes.
The decision and local prerequisites are documented.

tasks.title: Scaffold the application
acceptance_criteria: The application starts successfully from the agenza Conda environment.
Development, build, test, and lint commands are available.
The repository ignores generated files, dependencies, build output, and local secrets.

tasks.title: Create the main two-pane interface
acceptance_criteria: The main window displays two clearly separated terminal panes.
Both panes remain usable when the window is resized.
The layout has clear focus and active-pane states.

tasks.title: Implement the terminal process layer
acceptance_criteria: The app can start an interactive PTY process for each pane.
Input, output, terminal resizing, and Unicode text work correctly.
The two PTY processes are isolated from one another.

tasks.title: Connect both terminal panes to their PTY processes
acceptance_criteria: Typing in either pane sends input only to its own process.
Output from each process appears only in its own pane.
Common terminal controls, colors, cursor movement, scrolling, copy, and paste work.

tasks.title: Launch Codex in both terminals
acceptance_criteria: Each pane starts the Codex CLI through the agenza Conda environment.
Both Codex sessions can run at the same time and accept input independently.
A missing Conda environment or Codex installation produces a useful error message.

tasks.title: Add project-folder selection
acceptance_criteria: The user can select the working directory used by the Codex sessions.
Both terminals clearly show which project folder they are using.
Invalid or inaccessible folders are handled without crashing.

tasks.title: Add terminal session controls
acceptance_criteria: Each terminal can be restarted independently.
The user can clear the visible terminal output.
Unexpected process exits are shown in the affected pane with a restart action.

tasks.title: Handle application and process lifecycle safely
acceptance_criteria: Closing the app terminates both child process trees cleanly.
Restarting one session does not affect the other session.
The app does not leave orphaned Codex or shell processes after exit.

tasks.title: Add essential keyboard and accessibility behavior
acceptance_criteria: The user can switch focus between terminals with the keyboard.
Terminal text is readable and the active pane is visually identifiable.
Standard terminal keyboard shortcuts are not accidentally intercepted by the app.

tasks.title: Add application logging and user-facing error handling
acceptance_criteria: Startup and process failures provide concise recovery instructions.
Diagnostic logs are stored locally without recording terminal input or secrets.
An error in one terminal does not crash the whole application.

tasks.title: Add automated tests
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover process startup, input and output routing, resize events, restart behavior, and cleanup.
A smoke test verifies that two independent terminal sessions can run concurrently.
All automated tests pass in the agenza Conda environment.

tasks.title: Perform manual release testing
acceptance_criteria: Both Codex sessions complete a real interactive workflow independently.
Copy, paste, scrolling, resizing, focus switching, restart, and app shutdown are verified.
Missing prerequisites and process crashes are verified.
No orphaned processes remain after repeated open and close cycles.

tasks.title: Create a distributable application build
acceptance_criteria: A clean machine can install or run the packaged application.
The app detects and explains missing Conda or Codex prerequisites.
The packaged build opens two working Codex terminals.

tasks.title: Finish release documentation
acceptance_criteria: The README includes setup, development, build, install, and usage instructions.
Required versions of Conda, the agenza environment, and Codex are documented.
Known limitations and troubleshooting steps are documented.

tasks.title: Prepare and publish release 0.1.0
acceptance_criteria: The version number and changelog are finalized.
All release checks pass from a clean checkout.
The distributable build and release notes are published.
